title: smartbook.json
description: A smart ebook's descriptor. The same format backs a bundled book under books/<slug>/ and a portable .smartbook package. A book is data only — there is no code file.

schemaVersion.description: Schema version this descriptor is written against. This build writes 2 and reads 1–2.

minReaderSchema.description: Oldest reader schema able to render this package. Defaults to schemaVersion. Set it when a newer package is still readable by an older reader.

slug.description: Stable identifier, lowercase with hyphens. Must match the book's folder name.

description.description: One-line summary, shown on the shelf.

cover.description: Cover image as a packaged asset path, e.g. assets/cover.png. The file must exist in the book folder.

engine.description: Engine compatibility range. Advisory only — nothing enforces it.

chapters.description: Chapters in order. If omitted, they are derived from content/: a numeric filename prefix sets the order and the first heading sets the title.

part.description: The id of a part declared in `parts`. Omit for a chapter that sits outside the grouping, such as a preface or an appendix.

parts.description: Named groups of chapters, e.g. 'Part I — Foundations'. Referenced by chapters[].part. A part appears where its first chapter appears, and one no chapter claims is not drawn.

assets.description: Declared asset paths. Each must exist in the book folder.

islands.description: The interactive islands this book uses.

packs.description: Island packs beyond the built-ins, keyed by pack name, with per-book options. The platform maps a name to its implementation; the book carries only data.

required.description: Canonical island names the content uses. Written automatically on export — you do not need to maintain this by hand.

visibility.description: Publication intent. Required: absent or unrecognised counts as private, and the build refuses to run when anything under books/ is not public. 'private' books belong in a separate repository and ship as .smartbook packages.
